question: Can a streaming neural encoder-decoder codec with residual vector quantization and a simple spectrogram adversary beat Opus, EVS and Lyra-v2 in human-rated quality at low bitrates, in real time?
hypothesis: A single multiscale STFT discriminator plus a gradient loss balancer gives a simpler, more stable training than prior codecs and yields better perceptual quality at equal bandwidth.
contributions: Streaming encoder-decoder codec with quantized latent space trained end to end, 24 kHz mono and 48 kHz stereo
Single multiscale STFT (MS-STFT) discriminator as perceptual loss
Loss balancer where a weight is the fraction of the gradient a loss represents
Small Transformer language model plus arithmetic coding cutting bandwidth by up to 40%
Extensive MUSHRA evaluation and ablations over speech, noisy-reverberant speech and music

method.summary: EnCodec is a convolutional encoder (4 blocks, strides 2,4,5,8, 2-layer LSTM), an RVQ with up to 32 codebooks of 1024 entries, and a mirrored decoder, trained with time and mel-frequency L1/L2 reconstruction, MS-STFT hinge adversarial loss, feature matching and commitment loss, with a gradient balancer. An optional 5-layer Transformer LM over the codes drives a range coder for further compression.
method.task: neural audio compression (lossy codec) with variable bandwidth

datasets.name: DNS Challenge 4 (speech)
datasets.split: 98% train, 1% valid, 1% test of clean segments

datasets.name: AudioSet
datasets.split: unbalanced train segments for train; half of eval for valid, half for test

datasets.name: FSD50K
datasets.split: dev set for train; eval split between valid and test

datasets.name: Jamendo
datasets.split: 96% of artists train, 2% valid, 2% test, no artist overlap
datasets.preprocessing: 48 kHz stereo model trained on music only

other.codebooks: at most 32 (16 at 48 kHz), 10 bits each
other.bandwidths: 1.5, 3, 6, 12, 24 kbps at 24 kHz; 3, 6, 12, 24 kbps at 48 kHz

models.name: EnCodec 48 kHz stereo
models.architecture: same as 24 kHz, non-streamable, discriminator STFT windows doubled

models.name: EnCodec entropy-coding LM
models.architecture: causal Transformer, one embedding table and one linear head per codebook
models.context: 3.5 s causal receptive field, trained on 5 s sequences

models.name: MS-STFT discriminator
models.architecture: 5 identical 2D conv nets on complex STFT

other.kernel: 3x8 first conv, 32 channels, dilation 1,2,4 in time, stride 2 on frequency, final 3x3

models.name: Lyra-v2 (SoundStream)
models.architecture: neural codec, official Lyra 2 at 3.2 and 6 kbps on audio upsampled to 32 kHz

models.name: SoundStream reimplementation
models.architecture: RVQ with STFTD+MSD discriminators, relative feature loss, layer norm in discriminators

training.objective: LG = lt*L1 time + lf*mel L1/L2 (64 bins, scales 2^5..2^11, hop window/4) + lg*hinge adversarial + lfeat*relative feature matching + lw*RVQ commitment; discriminator hinge loss
training.regularisation: loss balancer R=1, beta=0.999; discriminator updated with probability 2/3 at 24 kHz and 0.5 at 48 kHz; per-bandwidth discriminator

other.data mixing: s1 Jamendo single 0.32; s2 other single 0.32; s3 mix of two 0.24; s4 mix of three non-music 0.12
other.augmentation: random gain -10 to 6 dB, clipped samples rejected, reverb with prob 0.2, RT60 in [0.3,1.3] except single-source music
other.bandwidth sampling: number of codebooks random multiple of 4
other.range coder: probabilities rounded to 1e-6, total range width 2^24, minimum range width 2

inference.decoding: range-based arithmetic coding with LM probabilities (entropy coding option)
inference.samples: 50 random 5 s samples per test category for MUSHRA, at least 10 annotations per sample

other.latency: 13.3 ms at 24 kHz streaming; 1 s at 48 kHz

metrics.name: MUSHRA
metrics.definition: crowd-sourced ratings 1 to 100 with hidden reference and low anchor; annotators dropped if reference rated under 90 in at least 20% of cases or anchor above 80 more than 50% of time

metrics.name: Real time factor
metrics.definition: duration of audio divided by processing time; >1 is faster than real time

eval.protocol: Test categories: clean speech (DNS), clean speech mixed with FSD50K, Jamendo music, proprietary music. RTF profiled on a single thread of a MacBook Pro 2019 CPU at 6 kbps. No seeds or repeated training runs reported.

availability.data: public datasets except proprietary music set

evidence.quote: We train all models for 300 epochs, with one epoch being 2,000 updates
For the 48 kHz model, we use instead λg = 4, λfeat = 4.

limits: Authors say the entropy-coding probabilities were rounded to 1e-6 because batch and streaming evaluation differ by more than 1e-8, and that more contexts would be needed before deployment.
48 kHz model is slower than real time with entropy coding and has 1 s latency due to normalisation.
Entropy coding adds latency (about 13 ms more) and is slower, so it is suited to non-low-latency use.
Compression gain from the small LM shrinks at higher bandwidths.
Compared against the official Lyra-v2, not the original SoundStream, which is not open sourced; the SoundStream comparison uses a reimplementation with the same hyperparameters.
No number of training seeds or run-to-run variance reported; MUSHRA CIs only.
Only quality of reconstruction is evaluated; use as tokens for language models is not tested.

terms.definition: each loss weight defines the fraction of the overall gradient it should represent, decoupling the weight from the typical scale of the loss
the ratio between the duration of the audio and the processing time, so that it is greater than one when the method is faster than real time
